notes: Tier 1 (direct HTTP fetch, curl with a real browser UA) succeeded for all checks; no Playwright/Chrome needed. robots.txt checked first: explicit 'User-agent: ClaudeBot / Allow: /' (also GPTBot, PerplexityBot etc all allowed) - no opt-out, proceeded. robots.txt disallows /search* for crawling so the internal search box was not used; relied on nav + taxonomy facet data instead, which is more reliable anyway per project lessons on site-search false-absence. Category sitemap (sitemap_2-category.xml) returned a Cloudflare 403 challenge page but was not needed since direct page fetches worked. Fetched homepage (200, 786KB) and extracted the full server-rendered global nav (~206 unique category links spanning Furniture/Lighting/Home Decor/Outdoor/Bathroom/Rugs/Tabletop etc.) - zero Christmas/Halloween/Diwali/Easter/Valentine/Thanksgiving/New Year/Mother's Day/Father's Day links present anywhere in it. Specifically fetched /outdoor-lighting/ (1.9MB) given Lumens is lighting-focused per task instructions - grepped for all holiday keywords, found only two false positives ('Mother Nature' marketing copy, 'clean seasonally' FAQ text), no Christmas Lighting / Holiday Lighting category or subcategory anywhere on that page or in the nav's outdoor-lighting subtree (deck-and-step-lights, landscape-lighting, path-lights, well-lights, bollard-lights, spot-and-flood-lights, outdoor-wall-lights, etc. - none holiday-named). Fetched /gift-guide/ (editorial page, correctly excluded as a landing/gift-guide page per rules) but its embedded product-search JSON exposed the site's FULL category-refinement tree (every 'Home Furnishings > ... ' / 'Lighting > ...' / 'Outdoor & Landscape > ...' node with counts) - this is authoritative taxonomy evidence. Across that entire tree there is exactly ONE seasonal/holiday node: 'Home Furnishings > Decor & Accessories > Decorative Accessories > Holiday Accessories' (site displayNameOption 'Holiday Decor'). No Halloween/Thanksgiving/Easter/Diwali/Valentine/New Year/Mother's Day/Father's Day node exists anywhere in this tree - explicitly checked per task instructions that Mother's/Father's Day are in-scope and must be evaluated on merits, not excluded by default; they simply do not exist in Lumens' taxonomy. Resolved the flat URL for that node: https://www.lumens.com/holiday-accessories/ (200, title 'Holiday Decor | Ornaments & Christmas Decorations at Lumens.com', h1 'Holiday Decor', displayed '174 Results' - a genuine PLP with product grid). That page exposes 6 'FEATURED FILTER' category tiles (data-facet-product-category='Holiday Accessories'), each its own real PLP with its own URL and own displayed result count, all Christmas-themed (ornaments, figurines, decor, drinkware, entertaining/tabletop, serveware) - fetched each directly and read its own h1 + 'N Results' count. Their counts sum to 202, more than the parent's 174, confirming they are overlapping filtered subsets of the 174-item parent rather than a clean partition - so the parent 'Holiday Decor' is recorded as a grouping row (qty null) to avoid double-counting, and the 6 children are recorded with their own real qty/links. No standalone Halloween/Thanksgiving/Easter/Diwali/Valentine/New Year/Mother's/Father's Day content was found anywhere on the Holiday Decor page or its children (only one incidental product literally named 'New Year Firework Disc Ornament' - a single SKU name, not a category - so not recorded as a row). As a secondary/negative signal only (not treated as proof, since a nonsense control slug also returned 410), legacy-looking slugs /christmas-lighting/, /holiday-lighting/, /outdoor-christmas-lighting/, /mothers-day-gifts/, /fathers-day-gifts/, /valentines-day/, /halloween-decor/ all return HTTP 410 Gone - consistent with the nav/taxonomy evidence that no dedicated Christmas Lighting or other-holiday category currently exists on the site (Lumens appears to have discontinued a lighting-specific holiday category at some point, but nothing seasonal-lighting is live today). Conclusion: Lumens' only genuine, currently-live seasonal taxonomy is a Christmas-focused 'Holiday Decor' home-decor-accessories category with 6 real sub-PLPs; no Christmas Lighting, no other holiday, and no Mother's/Father's Day PLPs exist.
